# html_gpu_render

> Render an HTML page or a canvas animation frame by frame to raw, PNG or EXR frames for video, without
> screenshots: Chromium HTML-in-Canvas (whole page) or a GPU copy of a canvas, WebGPU readback, hidden Electron
> window. Optional motion blur from sub-frames summed on the GPU, optional HDR / float output. No dependencies.

Use it instead of a Puppeteer / Playwright screenshot loop when the screenshot is the bottleneck: measured 6.5 ms
against 61 ms per 3440 x 1440 frame. Experimental: it depends on a Chromium API that is still changing.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): everything. Sections: Quick start, Which mode (element / canvas / screenshot, canvas
  roads), The page contract (`window.__seek(t)`), CLI, API, Output (formats, alpha), Motion blur by sub-frames,
  HDR and float output (sources, colour, ffmpeg HEVC PQ recipe), How it works, Versions and the API rename
  (Chromium 150 vs 157), Measured numbers, Fidelity against a screenshot, Known limits, Failure messages, Tools
  and tests.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the same essentials in one page: how to run, the page contract, which mode, formats,
  traps, source layout.

## Entry points

- [bin/html-gpu-render.mjs](bin/html-gpu-render.mjs): the command line (`--help` lists every option).
- [src/index.mjs](src/index.mjs): `render(options)` and `DEFAULTS`.
- [src/driver.cjs](src/driver.cjs): the frame loop; its header comment describes the roads, the ring, the
  sub-frame sum and the float pass.

## Examples

- [demo/page.html](demo/page.html): an HTML / SVG page with a seek hook (element mode).
- [demo/motion.html](demo/motion.html): fast motion, for `--subframes`.
- [demo/canvas.html](demo/canvas.html), [demo/canvas_webgpu.html](demo/canvas_webgpu.html): canvas mode.
- [demo/hdr_webgpu.html](demo/hdr_webgpu.html), [demo/hdr_webgl.html](demo/hdr_webgl.html): float sources.

## Checks

- [test/run.mjs](test/run.mjs): `npm test`, the invariants claimed in the README.
- [tools/probe.mjs](tools/probe.mjs): what a given Electron or browser binary exposes.
- [tools/compare.mjs](tools/compare.mjs): pixel differences between two renders.
